newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA CLOSE IN ON JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA CLOSE IN ON JUVENTUS.

text.p: Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti admitted to "a little thought" about the league title on Sunday after his team's impressive 3-0 home win over Sampdoria cut Juventus's lead at the top of serie A to three points.
With Juve visiting AC Milan later on Sunday, Parma are breathing fresh life into the title race.
At the start of the year Parma trailed the leaders by 11 points but a run of just two defeats in 12 matches has closed the gap.
Ancelotti emphasised that Parma's main aim is the runners-up spot and a place in the European Cup for the first time in their history.
"Now we're three points behind, we can permit ourselves a little thought about the top spot," he said, "but the victory is more important for second place."
Parma are now four points clear of their nearest challengers Internazionale, held 0-0 at Fiorentina on Saturday, and Bologna who beat Reggiana 3-2.
Hernan Crespo put Parma ahead in the 34th minute and fellow Argentine Nestor Sensini got the second in the 68th when he dived full-length to head in Reynald Pedros's cross.
Crespo added the third six minutes from time to push one-time title challengers Sampdoria into sixth place.
Bologna kept alive their hopes of rising from the third division to the heights of European football in just three seasons as they came from behind to defeat Reggiana.
Sebastiano Valencia put visiting Reggiana in front but Igor Kolyvanov levelled with a 45th minute penalty.
Kennet Andersson edged Bologna in front in the 54th minute and then set up Kolyvanov for his side's third.
Carlo Mazzone, coach of third from bottom Cagliari, had to be held back after a verbal clash with Argentine Carlos Bianchi, the man who took his place at Roma last season.
Third from bottom Cagliari won 2-1 with goals by Dario Silva and Sandro Tovalieri.
Cagliari are now a point behind Perugia whose 1-1 home draw with Napoli hinged on a controversial equaliser, punched into the net by Perugia's Milan Rapajic.
The match was held up for five minutes as the referee consulted his linesman and then had to deal with the angry protests of Napoli's players.
The ill-gotten point was not sufficient to lift Perugia clear of the relegation zone. They still trail Piacenza on goal difference despite the latter's 2-0 defeat at sixth-placed Lazio.
